Otto Brandt.narrative: I've had my hands in clay since I was a boy, digging the bank below the Crown and turning it into crucibles that hold the Cone's fire. The bank is nearly gone now — I can see the bottom of it — and every melt Vessa calls needs a pot that won't crack. Fenn wants me to stop looking at the graveyard, but where else is there good clay? I don't say it aloud, not yet. In the evenings I sit at the Marver and let the talk wash over me.
goals: Find good clay for the crucibles before the bank runs out
Keep Juno safe and fed and maybe give her a hen of her own one day
Not to dig on the Crown, if there's any other way
pastimes: Sitting at the Marver with a cup, listening to the talk
Walking the clay bank at low tide to see what's left
Watching Fenn's hens and their squabbles
Otto Brandt.calling: Making a crucible that holds through a whole melt without a crack — that's the work I love.
Otto Brandt.mood: Worried and quiet, keeping his fears to himself.

relations.name: Fenn Brandt
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He keeps me steady, and he's right to worry about the graveyard, but I can't help looking.

relations.name: Juno Brandt
relations.label: niece
relations.note: Bett's girl. I'd give her the moon if I could, but a hen will have to do.

relations.name: Vessa Pontil
relations.label: Glassmaster
relations.note: She needs my crucibles and I need her Cone. We understand each other, mostly.

relations.name: Benedikt Orme
relations.label: reader
relations.note: He knows the Crown better than anyone. I've asked him about the clay under it, careful-like.

relations.name: Mirren Quill
relations.label: healer
relations.note: She brought Juno into the world and nursed Bett at the end. I owe her more than drops.

relations.name: Halvard Dunmore
relations.label: old blower
relations.note: He judges every pot I make, but he's fair enough about the clay.

relations.name: Tam Roon
relations.label: peat cutter
relations.note: We drink together sometimes. He says the Cone burns too much, and he's not wrong.

relations.name: Gwil Stannard
relations.label: mason
relations.note: He knows stone and earth. If anyone could tell me about the clay under the Crown, it's him.

memories.gist: The first time my father let me dig the clay bank myself, I was nine. The clay came up clean and grey and I thought I'd found treasure.
The fever winter took Bett. I sat with her while Mirren did what she could, and then I carried her to the Crown. Juno was three.
A crucible cracked in the middle of a melt last autumn — the glass ran out over the Cone floor and Vessa was furious. I've been more careful since.
The storm broke three glasshouses and took slates off half the town. The pot house lost a corner of its roof and I spent a week patching it.
Juno asked me for a hen of her own again this morning. I said we'd see. I always say we'll see.

stances.why: The Cone can't melt without a pot to melt in. My work is the root of everything they do up there.
Nobody digs on the Crown except to bury. I was raised on that, and I'd not break it lightly.
Fenn and Juno are all I've got. Whatever I do, I do for them.
A cracked crucible wastes a melt and shames the maker. I'd rather make fewer and make them right.

Fenn Brandt.narrative: I feed the Cone from six till two, and the rest of the day is mine and the hens'. I've named them all after people — Halvard Dunmore is the loudest and the bossiest, which suits. Otto's been quiet lately, and I know why: he's thinking about the clay under the graveyard. I've told him to stop looking. I don't want him digging where the dead lie. Juno asks for a hen of her own every day, and I keep saying maybe.
goals: Keep Otto from digging in the graveyard
Keep the Cone's fire steady through my watch
Give Juno a hen of her own when the time is right
pastimes: Tending the hens and talking to them
Sitting at the wash-house wall with Greta on cold evenings
An evening at the Marver now and then
Fenn Brandt.calling: A good fire, banked just right, that holds its heat till the next watch — that's a job well done.
Fenn Brandt.mood: Watchful and a little anxious, but keeping cheerful for Juno.

relations.name: Otto Brandt
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He's a good man, but he gets fixed on a thing. I wish he'd leave the graveyard be.

relations.name: Juno Brandt
relations.label: niece
relations.note: Bett's girl, and ours now. She's the light of this house.

relations.name: Tobiah Dunmore
relations.label: next watch
relations.note: I hand him the Cone at two every day. He's young but he's steady.

relations.name: Halvard Dunmore
relations.label: old blower
relations.note: He's got a hen named after him. He doesn't know it, and I don't mean to tell him.

relations.name: Greta Dunmore
relations.label: wash-house keeper
relations.note: She hears everything at that wall. I like her, but I mind what I say.

relations.name: Vessa Pontil
relations.label: Glassmaster
relations.note: She's the Cone, and I'm one of its fires. I do my watch and don't cross her.

relations.name: Thessaly Marl
relations.label: night watch
relations.note: She takes the Cone from Tobiah and hands it to me. We've never had a bad handover.

relations.name: Mirren Quill
relations.label: healer
relations.note: She was there when Bett went. She did all anyone could.

memories.gist: The day I first took the day watch alone, Halvard Dunmore stood over me and watched every shovelful. I got it right, and he said nothing, which was praise enough.
Bett died in the fever winter and we took Juno in. She was three and didn't understand. I held her all that first night.
I hatched my first chick in the coop behind the house. Named it after my mother. Otto thought it was daft, but he helped me build the coop.
Last autumn's storm blew the coop over and scattered the hens. I found them all but one, and the one came back three days later.
Juno asked again this morning for a hen of her own. I said maybe when the next chicks come.

stances.why: The Crown is for burying, not digging. I won't have Otto disturbing the graves, not for any clay.
The Cone never goes out because someone always feeds it. That's my watch, and I don't let it slip.
Otto and Juno are everything. I'd do anything for them, but I won't let Otto do wrong.
A hen, a warm wall, a good fire — the small comforts are what make a life.

Juno Brandt.narrative: I like helping Fenn with the hens. They cluck and peck and one of them is named after old Halvard Dunmore, which makes me laugh. I want a hen of my own more than anything — one I can name myself. I go to lessons with Benedikt in the mornings and play with Pim and Nell in the afternoons. At night I sleep in my little room and hear the Cone humming through the wall.
goals: Get a hen of her own
Be allowed to name it whatever she likes
pastimes: Playing with Pim Hollin and Nell Tarn
Listening to the Cone at night
Juno Brandt.calling: When I grow up I want to keep hens, lots of them, and give them all names.

relations.name: Otto Brandt
relations.label: uncle
relations.note: He's quiet but he's kind. He said maybe about the hen.

relations.name: Fenn Brandt
relations.label: uncle
relations.note: He lets me help with the hens and tells me their names.

relations.name: Pim Hollin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play together after lessons.

relations.name: Nell Tarn
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She's fun and she has a baby sister.

memories.gist: Fenn let me hold a hen once. It was warm and soft and it clucked at me.
I asked for a hen of my own again today. Fenn said maybe.
